objective: Harmonize blood glucose across Diabetes/Stroke/CKD (ages 30-70, glucose>0), test group differences with Kruskal-Wallis + Dunn post-hoc (Bonferroni), produce output.csv and output.png.

CKD.parsing: manual @data parse, '?' -> NaN, 1 malformed row (25-field mismatch after trailing-comma cleanup) dropped; 399 parsed

data_harmonization.units: all three glucose fields are mg/dL -> pooled without rescaling
data_harmonization.filtering: coerce numeric -> drop NaN age/glucose -> keep 30<=age<=70 -> drop glucose<=0
data_harmonization.artifact: harmonized_glucose_filtered.csv (4464 rows; re-derived from raw sources and written to workspace, identical group counts/stats to the upstream version)

statistics.posthoc_method: Dunn (1964) on pooled ranks with average-tie ranking and pooled tie correction (sigma^2 = N(N+1)/12 - sum(t^3-t)/(12(N-1))); two-sided normal p via erfc(|z|/sqrt2); Bonferroni x3 applied to p_value column; cross-validated against scikit-posthocs.posthoc_dunn (raw p Diabetes-CKD = 0.66166 both)
statistics.interpretation: Kruskal-Wallis rejects equality of the three glucose distributions (H=628.13, p=4.01e-137). Post-hoc: Diabetes and CKD do not differ (median 125 vs 123 mg/dL, p_adj=1.0), while Stroke has markedly lower glucose (median 92.23) than both Diabetes and CKD (both p_adj < 1e-36). CKD shows the highest mean (151.2) and widest spread (IQR 100-169, max 490), Diabetes is highest by median but truncated at 199 in source data, Stroke is lowest and tightest.
statistics.limitations: Measurement semantics differ (Diabetes = 2h OGTT plasma glucose, Stroke = long-run average glucose, CKD = random non-fasting bgr); with N=4464 tiny differences reach significance (effect size epsilon^2=0.14 -> moderate); Diabetes glucose is capped at 199, compressing its upper tail.

output.png.plot: overlaid density histogram, bins=50, alpha=0.6, Diabetes=red, Stroke=blue, CKD=green
output.png.annotation: Kruskal-Wallis H=628.13, p=4.012e-137 shown on figure + legend with n/median, x clipped at pooled 99.5th percentile

execution_notes: matplotlib had to be reached via site.getusersitepackages() because the interpreter runs in isolated mode (-I)
all statistics deterministic; re-running reproduces identical values
